claims.text: Dynamic loading promotes stress-induced local rearrangement and formation of transient stacking-fault networks in high-entropy alloys.
Stacking-fault networks seed nanotwinning.
Stacking-fault networks seed an fcc-to-hcp phase transformation in Cantor-like HEAs.
The stress-induced fcc-to-hcp transformation is reversible.
Concentration waves or intrinsic chemical heterogeneity produce fluctuations in lattice friction that promote stacking-fault networks.
Stress fluctuations during rapid loading locally reduce the stacking-fault energy.
Localized reductions in stacking-fault energy trigger transient short-range order.
Nanotwins and hcp domains impede dislocation motion and thereby increase strength.
Nanotwinning and the fcc-to-hcp transformation provide additional pathways for plastic strain and preserve ductility.
Continuous in situ phase transformation can make the dominant contribution to strain hardening in a dual-phase Cantor-like HEA.
Relative to quasi-static loading, dynamic loading will produce higher strain-hardening rates and strength while maintaining or improving ductility.
Relative to quasi-static loading, dynamic loading will produce a higher density of stacking faults, nanotwins, or hcp domains.
Quasi-statically loaded material has fewer stacking-fault networks, twins, and hcp domains and consequently lower strain hardening.
Equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi is a single-phase fcc HEA that combines strength and ductility.
Equiatomic CrCoNi is single-phase fcc and exhibits high cryogenic strength, ductility, and fracture toughness.
Networks of nanotwins have been observed in CrCoNi and CrMnFeCoNi following extensive deformation.
The proposed dynamic mechanism should operate primarily in chemically heterogeneous HEAs with low stacking-fault energy.
The mechanism should hold from ambient to cryogenic temperatures in alloys such as CrCoNi.
Alloys lacking chemical heterogeneity or low stacking-fault energy may not show the proposed dynamic behavior.
The relative quantitative contributions of transient hcp formation and nanotwinning to the mechanical response are unresolved.
